reference: Independent references, none derived from the tool: NIST SRD 144 atomic weights and isotopic compositions, downloaded from physics.nist.gov and parsed for this benchmark; ICRP Publication 74 (1996) Table A.42 ambient dose equivalent per unit neutron fluence, from two independent transcriptions both fetched and parsed here; IAPWS-95 water density via python-iapws 1.5.5 cross-checked with CoolProp 8.0.0; the ideal-gas law with CoolProp 8.0.0 as a real-gas cross-check; MCNP-5 manual Appendix H Watt fission-spectrum constants, fetched and parsed here; CODATA-2018 Boltzmann constant via scipy.constants.
reference_citations: NIST Standard Reference Database 144, "Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions for All Elements" (physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/Compositions/stand_alone.pl?ele=&ascii=ascii2&isotype=all), downloaded 2026-08-22 and parsed by /root/bench3/make_neutron_transport_ref.py. For the elements whose CIAAW standard atomic weight is an interval the tool value is required to equal the CIAAW conventional atomic weight, to be consistent with the abundance-weighted mean of the tabulated composition, AND to lie inside the published interval - the last of those three is new in this run.

ICRP Publication 74 (1996), Table A.42, H*(10) per unit neutron fluence, pSv cm2. GRADED transcription: SAND2009-1144 (Sandia National Laboratories, March 2009), MCNP de205/df205 card, converted from mrem/h per n cm-2 s-1 with the factor 3.6e-4 stated on the card. CROSSCHECK transcription: OSTI/ETDEWEB 20061540, Table 4 "Ambient Dose Equivalent per unit neutron fluence, pSv cm2, Publication 74" - this is a scan, and its OCR is accepted only where the energy token and the value token both parse with no character substitution and the value is within a factor of two of the graded transcription; 24 of 55 points fail that test and are recorded as unreadable rather than as disagreements.
IAPWS R6-95 (2018), evaluated with python-iapws 1.5.5 and cross-checked with CoolProp 8.0.0 (HEOS::Water).

X-5 Monte Carlo Team, "MCNP - A General Monte Carlo N-Particle Transport Code, Version 5", LA-UR-03-1987 rev. 2/1/2008, Appendix H, "Constants for the Watt Fission Spectrum", sections B.1 (neutron-induced) and B.2 (spontaneous fission). Downloaded from mcnp.lanl.gov and parsed for this run.

CODATA 2018 recommended value of the Boltzmann constant, via scipy.constants (8.617333262e-11 MeV/K, exact), and the exact SI Avogadro constant N_A = 6.02214076e23 /mol. The tool declares N_A x 1e-24 = 0.60221408 (the 2010 CODATA value) in its own model.equations; the reference uses the exact value instead, so the atom-density cases carry a 6.64e-9 relative offset that is recorded per material as avogadro_convention and is five orders of magnitude below the 1e-3 tolerance.

PNNL-15870 Rev.1, McConn et al., "Compendium of Material Composition Data for Radiation Transport Modeling" (2011) - the origin of the shipped reference densities and weight fractions; not re-fetched and not graded in this run.
tolerance: Chosen per quantity from the physics and from the tool's own printed precision, never from what makes the tool pass. Standard atomic weight: 5e-4 relative. Natural abundance: 5e-4 absolute. Nuclide mass: 2e-6 relative. Fluence-to-dose coefficients: 1e-3 relative, the tabulated precision of ICRP-74 Table A.42. Watt parameters: 1e-6 relative because they are quoted constants; the closed-form mean energy <E> = 3a/2 + a^2 b/4 is compared with the mean energy the tool states, at 3 %. Densities are graded TWICE: the 4-decimal #densityInfo readout on the 2026-08-12 contract (1.2e-4 relative or 5e-5 absolute, whichever is looser; water 1e-3 relative) so the two runs are comparable, and the 6-decimal Diagram.record.build().outputs value at +/-1e-6 g/cm3 absolute - one unit in the last printed place - which is 50x tighter for a solid and 20000x tighter for a gas. Water keeps 1e-3 on both surfaces because the tool evaluates the IAPWS-95 saturated-liquid line times a fitted isothermal compressibility and that fit is only good to about 1e-3 over the 0.05-5 MPa region benchmarked here; tightening it would grade the fit against a model it does not claim. Atom densities: 1e-3 relative against the tool's printed five significant digits, computed with standard atomic weights, with the abundance-weighted-nuclide-mass convention recorded per material as convention_spread. Where two published references disagree by more than the tolerance the case is FLAGGED AND NOT GRADED (HARNESS.md) - that happens twice here, at 16 MeV in the dose table and for the Cf-252 Watt constants. Gas densities are graded against the ideal-gas law because that is the model the tool states it implements; the deviation from CoolProp is recorded, not graded. recommendation.why: Every one of the 251 graded cases passes against references re-derived from cited primary sources for this run, the run is deterministic across two processes and four browser contexts, and the driver is proved to have driven 23 distinct states. A transport tool whose transport is unmeasured is a prototype.
